title: Customer Intake Hub: SLA-driven scoring & PII-enriched routing for data-governance requests
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Design and ship an Intake Hub and automated scoring pipeline for customer data-governance requests (log redaction, retention windows, PII exports, audit exports). The hub must enrich incoming requests with PII sensitivity scoring, apply SLA-prioritized routing, and produce operator-ready response templates and escalation instructions for legal and infra teams.
problem_statement: Enterprise customers submit heterogeneous data-governance requests via support, account teams, or security portals. Current triage is manual, inconsistent in SLA adherence, and risks missing legal/regulatory escalations. We need an automated front-door that normalizes requests and ensures predictable routing and response times.
scope_in_scope:
- Intake Hub: normalized JSON schema for governance requests
- Automated enrichment: PII sensitivity detector + retention impact estimator
- SLA-driven scoring: assign priority and deadline based on customer tier, sensitivity, and compliance risk
- Routing: map to teams (Customer Success, Security, Runtime Eng, Legal) with suggested assignee and response template
- Operator UI: quick accept/reassign buttons with visibility into enrichment signals
out_of_scope:
- Automated fulfillment of retention or redaction (engineering work item separate)
- Changes to billing or contract language
- New legal policy drafting
acceptance_criteria: Intake Hub accepts requests from Support form, Security portal, and email and normalizes into the canonical schema
Enrichment service returns a PII-sensitivity score (low/medium/high) and estimated log volume impact within 10s for 95% of requests
SLA scoring rules produce a recommended SLA and deadline that matches PM-defined mapping for customer tiers
Routing engine populates a suggested team and escalation runway; operator can override and record reason
Pilot with two enterprise customers completed and SLA adherence measured for pilot tickets
proposed_workflow: 1) Ingest request -> 2) Normalize into canonical schema -> 3) Enrich (PII detector, retention estimator, cost impact estimator) -> 4) Score with SLA rules -> 5) Route to target queue with suggested response template and escalation runway -> 6) Track SLA and surface missed SLAs to ops dashboard
automated_scoring_rules: Base SLA = customer_tier mapping (Enterprise = 72h, Midmarket = 5 business days, Startup = 10 business days)
If PII-sensitivity == high -> escalate SLA to 48h and add Legal as auto-watch
If estimated affected log volume > 100GB/month -> mark as 'high-cost-change' and flag Runtime Eng
If request type == 'redaction' and origin == 'audit' -> fast-track to 24h review
Add +1 priority for requests coming from CISO or Legal email aliases
routing_rules: Legal: PII-sensitive exports, third-party subpoenas, or requests flagged with legal_regulatory=true
Runtime Eng (Dedicated/Private): retention or redaction changes that require infra config or on-prem tooling
Customer Success: low-risk retention window changes or clarifications for self-serve customers
Security Ops: incidents where request references breach or exfiltration
Cross-team assignments will include a required follow-up owner and SLA checkpoint
escalation_runway: T+24h: Auto-notify assignee and manager if no triage action taken
T+48h: Auto-add Legal watcher for high PII or regulatory requests
T+72h: Create an executive summary and notify CS leadership for enterprise customers whose SLA is breached
Emergency: If request references ongoing legal hold or subpoena, route to on-call Legal and Security immediately
metrics: False-positive rate of PII detector - tracked and target < 10%
% of requests auto-routed without manual edits - target >= 60%
Mean time from triage to resolution for redactions - baseline to be measured in pilot
stakeholders: Engineering: Marcus Chen (Assignee), Backend Team, Runtime Team
notes_and_tradeoffs: Tradeoff: Aggressive auto-routing increases throughput but risks misclassification; mitigated by audit logs and easy operator override
PII detection will initially use a heuristic model with human review loop; plan to iterate model after pilot
We prioritize predictable SLAs over immediate automation for legal cases — legal escalation always requires human confirmation
Retention estimator accuracy is coarse at launch; use conservative thresholds to avoid underestimating impact
progress_updates: 2026-03-01: Kickoff meeting with Engineering and Legal; aligned on canonical schema fields and sample events
2026-03-03: Prototype enrichment service (PII detector) returns results in ~6s for 95th percentile on staff test data
2026-03-06: Product/Legal decision: all high-PII exports require Legal watcher; accepted the slower SLA to ensure compliance
2026-03-09: Built wireframe for operator UI; CS reviewed and requested easy comments field and canned responses
2026-03-12: Pilot plan approved for two enterprise customers flagged by CS; next step implementation and consent forms
